title: An actor's own fields — software-analysis capability
description: The front matter of one actor, a file `ACT-<slug>.md` in `use-case-model/actors/` under the analysis location (software-analysis DEC-001 points 1 to 3): a named role that uses the system, and the needs it brings. The needs sit here, beside the description the body gives, so a tool reads them as data and never from the body (point 1). These are the actor's own fields: its friction block sits in the methodology's container beside them and is the core's, validated by the backbone (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). An actor anchors to where the software or a decision embodies it (DEC-001 point 4); one nothing embodies carries the reason it has none as `unanchored-because` in its friction block, the core's key, never among these fields (DEC-001 point 9; COR-050 point 1). Applied by the capability's check, `pkit software-analysis validate` (the `software-analysis:artefacts` member of `pkit validate`); unknown fields are refused, so a misspelt one is never silently ignored.

id.description: The actor's id, `ACT-` and the slug its file is named by. It never changes, and is never used again once the actor is withdrawn (DEC-001 point 3).

name.description: The actor's display name. The body's heading repeats it after the id, `# ACT-<slug> — <name>`, and the capability's check requires the two to match, so a reader of the front matter alone sees the name the page shows. It may change; the id does not.

needs.description: What the actor needs from the system, one line each. A user story — a need in one sentence — is an actor's need and a use case's goal, not an artefact of its own (DEC-001 point 1).
